Directions: Refer to the following excerpt, then answer each question that follows.
Content: “In the future `text(days)`, which we seek to make secure, we look forward to a world founded upon four essential human freedoms.
“The `text(first)` is freedom of speech and expression — everywhere in the world.
“The `text(second)` is freedom of every person to worship God in his own way — everywhere in the world.

“The `text(third)` is freedom from want — which, translated into world terms, means economic understandings which will secure to every nation a healthy peacetime life for its inhabitants-everywhere in the world.

“The `text(fourth)` is freedom from fear — which, translated into world terms, means a world-wide reduction of armaments to such a point and in such a thorough fashion that no nation will be in a position to commit an act of physical aggression against any neighbor — anywhere in the world.”
Copyright: President Franklin D. Roosevelt, State of the Union address, `text(January 1941)`
